summary: H.R. 6518, known as the Securing America's Fuels Act or SAF Act, amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to change tax credit calculations and extend timelines for sustainable aviation fuel. It reinstates specific credit amounts for sustainable aviation fuel produced at qualified facilities and extends the overall clean fuel production credit to cover fuel sold through December 31, 2033.

affected_groups.effect: Receive updated and extended tax credit amounts and calculations for qualifying fuel produced after December 31, 2025.

key_provisions: Reinstates a special rate calculation for sustainable aviation fuel by substituting 35 cents for 20 cents for certain qualified facilities.
Reinstates a special rate calculation by substituting $1.75 for $1.00 for other qualified facilities.

Defines sustainable aviation fuel as a liquid fuel, not including kerosene or fuel derived from palm fatty acid distillates or petroleum, sold for use in an aircraft and meeting specific ASTM International standards.
Extends the clean fuel production credit to apply to fuel sold after December 31, 2029, and through December 31, 2033.
Applies the amendments made by the Act to fuel produced after December 31, 2025.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the broader economic impact, exact cost to the government, or details on how many facilities will qualify.
The source text does not state the details of Public Law 119-21 beyond referencing its amendments to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

It reinstates specific credit amounts for sustainable aviation fuel produced at qualified facilities and extends the overall clean fuel production credit to cover fuel sold through December 31, 2033.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters tax credit calculations and extends the expiration date for the clean fuel production credit regarding sustainable aviation fuel through the end of 2033.
